title: Retention Curves, North Star Metrics, and the YC Growth Engine
content:
Lenny Rachitsky: Gustaf Alströmer spent five years running growth at Airbnb and is now a Group Partner at Y Combinator, having evaluated thousands of startups. Gustaf, when a startup comes to you asking how to grow faster, what is the first thing you look at?

Gustaf Alströmer: I look at exactly one graph: the cohort retention curve. If your retention curve does not flatten parallel to the x-axis, you do not have Product-Market Fit (PMF). Pouring money into growth, SEO, or paid ads before your retention curve flattens is like pouring water into a leaky bucket. You will churn every customer you buy.

Lenny Rachitsky: How do you know when a retention curve has flattened?

Gustaf Alströmer: You track cohorts over time—Week 1, Week 2, Week 4, Week 8. For consumer apps, if you retain 20-25% of users at Day 30 and that line stays flat, you have a solid business. For B2B SaaS, you want 60-80% annual retention. The moment that curve is horizontal, every single new user you acquire compounds your total active base. That is where exponential growth comes from.

Lenny Rachitsky: What metric framework do you teach founders at Y Combinator?

Gustaf Alströmer: We teach the hierarchy of metrics. At the top is your North Star Metric—which must measure the real value delivered to the customer, not just vanity revenue. Beneath the North Star are three inputs: Acquisition velocity, Activation percentage (completing the core setup), and Retention. Most founders obsess over acquisition when a 10% lift in activation yields a 50% compounding lift in long-term revenue.
